findings.description: The 'data' bucket is created with no ACL restriction, no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, and no restrictive bucket policy, and the inline comment states the bucket is public. Anyone on the internet could list and read its objects, including the customer master spreadsheet uploaded into it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects (including sensitive customer data) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No logging block is configured, so read/write access to this publicly exposed bucket is not recorded, preventing detection or forensic investigation of data exfiltration.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irrecoverably — an acute risk for a bucket that is publicly writable/readable and holds customer records.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false is attached, so sensitive objects in this public bucket may be retrieved over cleartext HTTP.

A file named 'customer-master.xlsx', evidently containing customer PII, is uploaded into the publicly readable, unencrypted 'data' bucket with no per-object encryption (no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption specified).
The financials bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial records are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured for the financials bucket, leaving no audit trail of access to sensitive financial data.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so financial objects can be overwritten or destroyed with no recovery path.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later object ACL or bucket policy change could expose financial data publicly with no account-level guardrail.
The operations bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so there is no record of who accessed objects in this bucket.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket, leaving it dependent solely on the private ACL to prevent public exposure.
The data_science bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so datasets are stored unencrypted despite a KMS key (aws_kms_key.logs_key) already existing in the account.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so a future public ACL or policy grant would not be blocked at the account/bucket level.

The central log destination bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no object lock or MFA delete, allowing an actor with Terraform or S3 delete permissions to destroy the audit trail covering the other buckets.

The log destination bucket has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; it uses a log-delivery-write ACL and holds request metadata that should be explicitly shielded from any public ACL or policy grant.
No bucket policy denies non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, permitting log objects to be transmitted in cleartext.
